chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-'Is ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Qurrat, from Mas'adah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He who fulfills his oath to them has not truly believed in Allah.

key_terms.بِيَمِينٍ: with an oath / by an oath
key_terms.وَفَى: to fulfill / to keep (an oath or promise)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to fulfill an oath in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the condition for true faith (Iman) is linked directly to the fulfillment of oaths made to others, highlighting the social dimension of belief in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith is often interpreted to mean that one who breaks an oath to a person has not truly anchored their faith in Allah, as their word is their bond with the Divine. It underscores the principle that religious piety is inseparable from personal integrity in dealings with creation.
